highlights: Nexus Auto can now use your own Anthropic and OpenAI keys. Save them once with `nexus auto --anthropic-api-key` and `nexus auto --openai-api-key` (each prompts for the key, so it never lands in your shell history), check them with `nexus auto`, and clear one with `nexus auto --unset openai-api-key`.

`nexus auto` shows all your keys in one place: saved on this machine, plus Provider Keys connected on your Fireworks account. Provider Keys work in every harness, a saved local key still wins for its provider, and `nexus auto` says so when Provider Keys are not enabled on your account.
`nexus status` now lists installed harnesses, and `nexus update` now updates Nexus CLI (`nexus upgrade` still works).
improvements: Turning on a harness that is not installed now fails with an explanation instead of writing settings for it.
Removed: `nexus claude live`. The status line shows the model and spend on every turn; `nexus claude usage` gives the full breakdown.

Fixed: Claude Code telemetry stays on so the Artifact tool shows up, too-old Claude Code warns instead of showing an empty picker, and the status line names the serving model. Running `nexus claude` again refreshes the picker.
Fixed: fewer keychain prompts (your keychain is read only when a command needs your key), and sign-in no longer tells account members they are not members.
Safer updates: if `~/.nexus` was not created by Nexus, `nexus update` stops before changing anything.
releases.footer: After upgrading, restart your harnesses to load the migrated settings.

highlights: FireConnect is now Nexus CLI. The command is `nexus` (it replaces `fireconnect`), and your data moves from `~/.fireconnect` to `~/.nexus` (the old path stays as a link). Your harnesses, key, and settings carry over unchanged. Try `nexus status`.
Environment variables are now `NEXUS_*` (`FIRECONNECT_*` still works). Rename them in your scripts and shell profiles when you get a chance.

FireRouter is retired. `nexus upgrade` moves every harness that was on a FireRouter route to `auto`, and picking a FireRouter model now fails with a pointer to `auto`: FireRouter routes are no longer supported. Use `--model auto` instead.

Narrow `auto` to Fireworks-hosted models only: `nexus auto --providers fireworks`. The setting is global, not per harness. `nexus auto --reset` restores the default. Claude Desktop and DeepSeek Harness support the setting too.
improvements: Claude Desktop works on Linux too: `nexus claude-desktop` routes Chat, Cowork, and Code through Fireworks there as well as on macOS.
releases.footer: After upgrading, restart your harnesses to pick up the new model settings.

highlights: Codex starts on FireRouter, and GPT turns run on your own sign-in. A fresh `fireconnect codex` picks `firerouter` and asks you to `codex login` with ChatGPT or an OpenAI key. Easy turns stay on open models, and the GPT models your sign-in offers sit right above the Fireworks catalog in `/model`. `fireconnect upgrade` switches existing setups over and keeps your model.

MCP servers and ChatGPT app connectors work in Codex. Their tools reach the model, so calls complete instead of the model saying a server "exposes no tools". `fireconnect upgrade` fixes existing setups.

Rotate your Fireworks key without breaking a harness. `fireconnect login` now saves the new key into every connected harness, VS Code included, even when you're already signed in. No more 401s from a harness holding the old key.

OpenCode v2 lists your Fireworks models. When `opencode.json` uses v2's `providers` map, FireConnect writes Fireworks there too, so `auto` and the rest show up in `/models` instead of silently going missing. `fireconnect upgrade` repairs existing setups.
improvements: Fixed: OpenCode's `/models` no longer lists routers like `glm-latest` twice. `fireconnect upgrade` cleans up existing configs.
Fixed: Claude Desktop works behind TLS-inspecting corporate proxies such as Zscaler. Re-run `fireconnect claude-desktop on` to pick it up.
Fixed: with Node from fnm, `fireconnect` could stop finding Node in new or non-interactive shells. Re-run the installer once to fix an existing install.
New: `fireconnect configure --unset openai-api-key` and `--unset anthropic-api-key` clear a saved provider key from FireConnect and from every harness holding a copy.
Clearer errors: when the model catalog can't load, you see the gateway's actual answer instead of a generic "reconnect to the network".

Heads-up: Claude Code no longer takes `--anthropic-api-key`. Claude turns already use Claude Code's own sign-in (`claude login` or an exported `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY`), and your next `fireconnect claude` removes any key an earlier version saved.

Heads-up: Codex no longer supports Azure/Foundry, because Codex CLI 0.160 removed the only transport Foundry offers. Run `fireconnect configure --provider fireworks` to put Codex back on the Fireworks gateway. OpenCode, Pi, Cursor, and VS Code still support Foundry.
releases.footer: After upgrading, restart Codex and OpenCode. If Codex asks you to sign in, run `codex login`.

highlights: Claude Desktop runs on Fireworks. On macOS, `fireconnect claude-desktop on` routes Chat, Cowork, and Code through Fireworks, starting on `auto`. Bring your connectors along with `fireconnect claude-desktop mcp sync`, and `off` puts your previous setup back exactly as it was.

Pin Claude Code tiers again. Keep Claude as your main model and hand subagents to an open model: `fireconnect claude --sonnet deepseek-flash-latest --subagent deepseek-flash-latest`. Re-running `on` keeps your pins, and `native` releases a slot.

FireRouter can reach OpenAI's frontier models. Save your key once with `fireconnect configure --openai-api-key sk-...`. It rides along only on FireRouter picks and is never required. Cursor, Copilot, and DeepSeek Harness can now pick plain `firerouter` too.

New Anthropic and OpenAI models show real dollars as soon as models.dev lists them. The status line, `fireconnect claude status`, and demo estimates read a cached price snapshot, so a model launch no longer waits on a FireConnect release. Offline, the last snapshot still prices your session.
improvements: Fixed: `fireconnect claude --model <id>` could report success without adding the model. It now becomes your default and shows up in `/model`, and your own picker rows stay untouched.
Fixed: Codex auto-review denied every approval. It called an OpenAI-only reviewer that Fireworks can't serve; now the model you picked does the review.
Fixed: `--model` on a first-time `on` left Codex with a one-model menu. You now get the model you asked for plus the full catalog.
Fixed: DeepSeek Harness 0.1.7 and later asked for a DeepSeek API key on first launch. It now goes straight to Fireworks.

Heads-up: Claude Code auto mode may show a "classifier requests are billed" notice once per session. Nothing is broken. Auto mode's safety checks run on your Sonnet model, so they bill to Anthropic unless you pin Sonnet with `fireconnect claude --sonnet <id>`.

New: `fireconnect models`, a shortcut for `fireconnect model list`. The list now says when to use each smart router: `auto` balances cost and quality, `auto-instant` is latency-first. If your account disables fast models, stay on `auto`.
releases.footer: Using Codex auto-review or DeepSeek Harness? Run `fireconnect codex on` or `fireconnect deepseek on` once after upgrading to pick up the fixes.

highlights: GitHub Copilot works with Fireworks. `fireconnect copilot-app` connects the desktop app, `fireconnect copilot-cli` the CLI. Your own models stay; `off` removes only what FireConnect added.
Claude Code keeps its own tier models. The Fireworks catalog is added to the `/model` picker instead of overriding slots. Older pinned slots are released on the next `fireconnect claude on`.
Every other harness starts on `auto`, the cost-aware mix, also selectable in every picker.
Claude Code web search and fetch go through Fireworks natively; the old `fireworks-websearch` MCP is removed on upgrade, your own MCPs untouched.
Codex web search works again; upgrade cleans up the 0.9.6 override.
improvements: The built-in Explore agent follows your session model again instead of always using Opus. Fixed on upgrade.
Pickers stay fresh: re-running `on` prunes retired models, adds new ones, and updates pricing and metadata. Upgrade refreshes the Claude picker too.
Codex auto-compacts at 80% of the context window so long sessions survive; GLM-5.3 models unlock max reasoning effort.

highlights: Codex 0.153 works with Fireworks again. It turns on a `web_search` tool the Responses API can't accept; FireConnect now bakes `web_search = "disabled"` and repairs existing setups on `fireconnect codex on`.
Cleaner cost breakdown: the status line and meter dedupe and name model labels instead of listing the same one twice.
improvements: Claude Fable 5.1 pricing added; estimates and `fireconnect model list` are accurate.
Subagent slot keeps its `[1m]` tag when routed.
`fireconnect model list` aligns price precision across models.
`fireconnect claude demo` disables your user MCPs so they can't skew the race.
releases.footer: Using Codex? Run `fireconnect upgrade` and 0.153 keeps working through Fireworks.

highlights: Session costs in your Claude prompt. A new status line shows which models ran, what they cost at Fireworks rates, and cache savings. Your own status line is left alone: `fireconnect claude off` restores everything.
ChatGPT desktop app support. `fireconnect chatgpt` and `fireconnect codex` share one config, so you route both through Fireworks with a single command. Quit the app first so its model list refreshes.

Smart router mixes (preview): pin `auto` for the default mix or `auto-instant` for latency-first routing. For example: `fireconnect claude --sonnet auto-instant`. Every `auto-*` slug works the same way.

Simpler Claude model setup. The wizard lets you pick a model per slot instead of toggling fast profiles. New installs default to Sonnet on `deepseek-pro-latest`, Opus on `glm-latest`, and Fable on vision-capable `glm-flash-latest`. FireRouter still lands on Opus at first connect when your key supports it.

Faster `fireconnect model list`. Results are cached for an hour, work offline, show when they were last updated, and `--refresh` pulls the latest. Smart Routers lists `auto`, `auto-instant`, and FireRouter.
improvements: MCP tool search works through the Fireworks gateway again. Upgrade applies the fix automatically.
`fireconnect claude demo` and the status line use the same pricing, so their numbers always match.
`fireconnect upgrade` repairs missing dependencies; partial installs recover instead of crashing.
Linux SSH/WSL: keys store in an encrypted file with timeouts on keyring and network calls. No more hangs.
`fireconnect claude status` shows every slot, including defaults you never explicitly set.
GLM 5.3 and GLM 5.3 Flash added. Stale pins no longer hide newer releases; US-only pricing corrected.
Claude picker lists `auto` on every slot and `auto-instant` on Sonnet only.
releases.footer: Already on Claude? Upgrade keeps your slot picks. Run `fireconnect claude --interactive` to adopt the new defaults. Legacy pins like `deepseek-v4-flash` move to `deepseek-flash-latest` on your next `fireconnect claude on`.

highlights: `fireconnect claude demo`: improved cost calculation and racing experience.
`fireconnect cursor on/off`: more robust; uninstall now waits for Cursor to quit before restoring, preventing broken state.
`fireconnect uninstall`: paced, harness-by-harness checklist that waits for IDEs to quit.
New Claude Code defaults: Sonnet on Anthropic's own model, Opus on `deepseek-pro-latest`, Haiku and subagents on `deepseek-flash-latest`. Change them with `fireconnect claude --interactive`.
Anthropic and Fireworks models both work once fireconnected. Mix them freely.
`fireconnect claude demo` races two live Claude Code sessions side by side.
DeepSeek Harness replaces Deep Agents: `fireconnect deepseek on`.
improvements: `fireconnect status` no longer reports "All off" while models are routed.
OpenCode shows per-model cost, and hides it for Fire Pass subscriptions.
releases.footer: Pinned `deepseek-v4-flash`? Your next `fireconnect claude on` moves it to `deepseek-flash-latest`.

highlights: Live session cost meter: watch Fireworks spend accumulate in a tmux split pane beside Claude Code, with a recent-session picker.
VS Code now uses the chat-completions API for better compatibility.
Cursor picker hides built-in models and preserves your native model IDs when re-enabling.
improvements: FireRouter model IDs are treated as 1M-context; Kimi K3 specs corrected to 1M with [1m] enabled for Claude.
Linux quit detection ignores Electron helper processes in VS Code.
Claude usage meter exits cleanly on quit.

highlights: Keep Claude Code connected when you reinstall or upgrade. On FireConnect 0.9.0 and newer, FireConnect no longer asks you to disconnect first. Your harness settings stay put.
When a newer FireConnect is available, interactive terminals can upgrade in place. Answer Yes to run `fireconnect upgrade`, or No to snooze for a day.
Claude model preferences now persist across sessions, with interactive onboarding and a fast-model profile toggle.
improvements: More reliable harness setup: baked API keys, Claude websearch MCP auth, and fewer Cursor / OpenCode / VS Code edge-case failures.
Clearer Claude model defaults and catalog labels, including Kimi K3 naming and pricing.
releases.footer: If you are upgrading from before 0.9.0 with Claude connected, FireConnect will still offer to restore your original settings first.

highlights: Find models in one place with `fireconnect model list`. The coding-focused catalog includes standard and fast options across model families.
FireRouter now works like any other model through `on --model firerouter`.
VS Code now uses the Fireworks Responses API. Vision-capable Kimi models accept image inputs, while GLM models remain text-only.
Web-search groundwork: FireConnect can configure the Fireworks-hosted WebSearch MCP for eligible accounts.
Claude usage reports now show session token usage and estimated Fireworks cost.
improvements: Improved sign-in with custom enterprise SSO support, secure credential storage, and upgrades.
Better preservation of user settings, headers, model selections, and backups.
More reliable Azure endpoint handling, Windows installation, and error guidance.
Privacy-safe request attribution without replacing native user agents.
releases.footer: Your existing harness settings are not changed during upgrade.
